LESSON: ACTING

Grade: Grade 10
Subject: THEATRE AND FILM
Strand: Production
Topic 2.1: Acting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 35

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Acting, part of Production in Grade 10 THEATRE AND FILM.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to engage in theatre games and exercises before a performance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. research and identify theatre games and exercises (vocal, physical, mind) used before performances,

2. participate in various theatre games and exercises,

3. read the selected script to understand the play,

4. interpret the script to perform the assigned character role,

5. watch live or recorded performances to improve acting skills,

6. memorise the lines of the assigned character role in the script,

7. watch videos of spoken words performances to identify performance elements essential for a spoken word performance, (voice, body, delivery) 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. research and identify theatre games and exercises (vocal, physical, mind) used before performances,
2. participate in various theatre games and exercises,
3. read the selected script to understand the play,
4. interpret the script to perform the assigned character role,
5. watch live or recorded performances to improve acting skills,
6. memorise the lines of the assigned character role in the script,
7. watch videos of spoken words performances to identify performance elements essential for a spoken word performance, (voice, body, delivery) 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Acting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: the learner develops verbal and non-verbal communication skills while performing.

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner develops focus and coordination through theatre games and exercises.

● Self-efficacy: the learner develops trust, self-confidence and self-esteem while performing before an audience.

● Digital Literacy: the learner develops digital skills while researching and recording performances.

Values:
● Patriotism: the learner develops a sense of nationhood through acting.

● Respect: the learner shows courtesy to team members and audience during acting.

● Unity: the learner works in collaboration with others during rehearsals and performance.

12

(PCIs):

● Global Citizenship: the learner acquires a sense of diverse world views from interacting with performances from other

parts of the world.

● Life Skills: the learner acquires negotiation and stress management skills during role play and de-roling.
